description:
FILED s411 (Fable) — found by a review probe while checking the Phase R fix (the flatten-list magic-cell copy).  NOT the plan's concern; filed per the structural-first rule (a found bug is FILED and jumps the queue only if it regresses a baseline or blocks a phase).

REPRO (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):
  my $c = 0; my $r = \$c; ++$$r; print "pre=$c\n";        # perl 1, PCL 0 + "PCL: statement dropped … ++$$r; -- Handle single node of unknown type"
  my $x = ++$$r; print "x=$x c=$c\n";                      # perl x=1 c=1, PCL x= c=0 (the whole `my` statement is dropped)
  my $y = ++${$r};                                          # same
  $$r++; --$$r; ${$r}++; $$r += 5; ++$$ar[0]; ++$hr->{k};   # all CORRECT

So the missing case is exactly: prefix ++/-- whose OPERAND BEGINS WITH A CAST (`$$r`, `${$r}`); the element forms `++$$ar[0]` work because the cast is followed by a subscript and takes a different path.  It is a #138-family drop (announced, statement replaced by nil) — i.e. Option B phase 2 territory: the operand grammar of a prefix operator (`docs/option-b-phase2-plan.md` B1/#372: "a named unary's operand may BEGIN with a named unary" — here a prefix op whose operand begins with a cast).  Check whether tools/drop-census.pl already lists the shape (perl-tests + perl t/); if not it is a population-ZERO shape and a Pl/t guard row is the bar.

Also probed while there (all fine, recorded so nobody re-probes): `bless \$c` scalar-ref objects deref-write correctly except through the same `++$$o` shape; a hash-based tie FETCH/STORE through list assignment matches perl after the s411 %p-flatten-list fix.
subject: `++$$r` / `--$$r` / `++${$r}` — a prefix inc/dec whose operand is a scalar-ref CAST is a whole-statement DROP (announced) in every position: `my $x = ++$$r` loses both the increment and the value; postfix `$$r++`, `$$r += 1`, `++$$ar[0]`, `++$hr->{k}` all work
